# @aszura/saltline-node

> Saltline API client for server-side JavaScript (Node.js 20+, Deno, Bun, edge workers). Connects
> end users' third-party accounts, calls those providers' APIs through Saltline, manages provider
> webhooks, and signs users in with OAuth2. Holds the secret API key: server-side only.

This file is for AI coding assistants. Follow the rules first; the reference follows.

## Rules

1. **Server only.** `new Saltline({ apiKey })` takes the secret key. Never import this package in
   browser or mobile code; use `@aszura/saltline-browser` there, which talks only to your backend.
2. **PKCE on every connect and sign-in.** `connections.init` / `sessions.init` take a
   `codeChallenge`; `claim` needs the matching `codeVerifier`. The connection or session is not
   live until claimed. Store the verifier where only the starting user's browser reaches it (their
   server session, or the browser's `sessionStorage` via `@aszura/saltline-browser`). **Never store
   it in a lookup keyed by `connectionKey` or `sessionKey`**, because the key appears in the redirect URL.
3. **Claim once.** `claim` is single-use and expires 30 minutes after the provider step. Delete the
   stored verifier before or right after claiming.
4. **Set `auth`, `redirectUrl` and the provider on the server.** If the browser picks a provider,
   check it against an allowlist.
5. **Branch on `error.code`, never `error.message`.** Unknown codes: fall back to `error.status`.
6. **Proxy responses are the provider's.** `proxy.fetch` returns a `Response` for every provider
   status (4xx/5xx included). Check `response.ok` yourself. Only Saltline's own refusals throw.
7. **Verify webhooks with the raw body**, before any JSON parsing. A re-serialized body won't verify.
8. Persist `connection.connectionKey` against your user after `claim`. It's the handle for every
   later proxy, refresh, revoke and webhook call.

## Install and create a client

```ts
// npm install @aszura/saltline-node
import { Saltline } from '@aszura/saltline-node';

const saltline = new Saltline({
  apiKey: process.env.SALTLINE_API_KEY!,
  // environment: 'staging',            // default 'production'
  // baseUrl: 'https://…/v1',            // overrides environment; include /v1
  // fetch: customFetch,                 // default globalThis.fetch
});
```

Base URLs: production `https://api.saltline.dev/v1`, staging `https://api-staging.saltline.dev/v1`
(exported as `BASE_URLS`).

## Connect a user's account (server-side PKCE)

```ts
import { createPkce, parseConnectionRedirect } from '@aszura/saltline-node';

// Start, e.g. POST /connect/google, behind your login:
const pkce = await createPkce();
const { authorizationUrl } = await saltline.connections.init('google', {
  auth: 'oAuth2',
  redirectUrl: 'https://yourapp.com/connected',
  codeChallenge: pkce.codeChallenge,
  codeChallengeMethod: pkce.codeChallengeMethod, // 'S256'
  externalUserId: user.id,                       // optional, your user id
});
req.session.saltlineConnect = pkce.codeVerifier;
res.redirect(authorizationUrl);

// Return, GET /connected, same browser session:
const result = parseConnectionRedirect(fullRequestUrl);
const codeVerifier = req.session.saltlineConnect;
delete req.session.saltlineConnect;
if (result.ok && codeVerifier) {
  const connection = await saltline.connections.claim('google', result.connectionKey, codeVerifier);
  await db.saveConnection(user.id, connection.connectionKey);
} else if (!result.ok) {
  // result.error, result.errorMessage: user declined or provider failed
}
```

If the browser makes the PKCE pair instead (no server session), the server exposes two endpoints:
start receives `{ codeChallenge, ... }` and answers `{ authorizationUrl, connectionKey }`; finish
receives `{ connectionKey, codeVerifier }` and calls `claim`. See `@aszura/saltline-browser`.

## Sign users in

```ts
const pkce = await createPkce();
const { sessionKey, authorizationUrl } = await saltline.sessions.init('google', {
  auth: 'oAuth2',
  redirectUrl: 'https://yourapp.com/signed-in',
  codeChallenge: pkce.codeChallenge,
  codeChallengeMethod: 'S256',
});
req.session.saltline = { sessionKey, codeVerifier: pkce.codeVerifier };
// redirect to authorizationUrl, then at /signed-in:
const pending = req.session.saltline;
delete req.session.saltline;
const { user, raw } = await saltline.sessions.claim('google', pending.sessionKey, pending.codeVerifier);
```

## Call a provider's API

```ts
const response = await saltline.proxy.fetch('trello', '1/members/me/boards', { connectionKey });
if (!response.ok) { /* provider error: inspect response.status / body */ }
const boards = await response.json();

await saltline.proxy.fetch('github', 'repos/acme/app/issues', {
  connectionKey,
  method: 'POST',
  body: { title: 'Bug' },          // sent as JSON
  query: { per_page: '50' },
  headers: { Accept: 'application/vnd.github+json' },
  // contentType: 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded', // format the provider receives
  // version: '2022-11-28',        // pin provider API version
  // integrationKey: '…',          // only if the provider has several integrations and no default
});
```

`path` is the provider's API path, without a leading host. It must be non-empty and contain no
`..` segment. Caller headers starting with `x-saltline-` are dropped.

Async: `await saltline.proxy.enqueue(provider, path, { connectionKey, callbackUrl })` returns
`{ requestId }` (HTTP 202). The provider's response is POSTed to `callbackUrl` (public HTTPS).
Verify that callback with `verifyWebhook`.

## Webhooks

```ts
import { verifyWebhook } from '@aszura/saltline-node';

// Express: app.post('/hooks/saltline', express.raw({ type: '*/*' }), handler)
const valid = await verifyWebhook(req.headers, req.body /* Buffer/raw string */, process.env.SALTLINE_SIGNING_SECRET!);
if (!valid) return res.sendStatus(401);
const event = JSON.parse(req.body.toString());
```

`secrets` may be an array during secret rotation. Default timestamp tolerance is 300 s
(`{ toleranceSeconds }` to change). `verifyWebhook` never throws; it returns false.

Manage subscriptions on a connection:

```ts
await saltline.webhooks.register('github', { connectionKey, kind: 'push', metadata: 'repo-42', body: { /* kind-specific */ } });
await saltline.webhooks.list('github', { connectionKey });
await saltline.webhooks.get('github', webhookKey, { connectionKey });
await saltline.webhooks.update('github', webhookKey, { connectionKey, body: { … } });
await saltline.webhooks.delete('github', webhookKey, { connectionKey });
const { ingressUrl, setupUrl } = await saltline.webhooks.initManual('stripe', { connectionKey, redirectUrl });
```

## API reference

All methods are async and throw `SaltlineError` on a Saltline error. `provider` is the provider key,
e.g. `'google'`. The optional `integrationKey` is only needed when a provider has several
integrations and no default.

| Call | Returns |
| --- | --- |
| `connections.init(provider, { auth, redirectUrl, codeChallenge, codeChallengeMethod: 'S256', externalUserId?, theme?: 'light' \| 'dark' }, { integrationKey? })` | `{ connectionKey, authorizationUrl, message? }` |
| `connections.claim(provider, connectionKey, codeVerifier)` | `Connection` |
| `connections.refresh(provider, connectionKey)` | `Connection` (throws `CONFLICT` if a refresh is running) |
| `connections.revoke(provider, connectionKey, { integrationKey? })` | `void` |
| `connections.list(provider, { integrationKey })` | `Connection[]` |
| `sessions.init(provider, { auth: 'oAuth2', redirectUrl, codeChallenge, codeChallengeMethod, externalUserId?, theme? }, { integrationKey? })` | `{ sessionKey, authorizationUrl, message? }` |
| `sessions.claim(provider, sessionKey, codeVerifier)` | `UserInfo` `{ user, raw }` |
| `sessions.userinfo(provider, sessionKey, { integrationKey? })` | `UserInfo` (live from provider) |
| `sessions.refresh(provider, sessionKey)` | `Session` |
| `sessions.revoke(provider, sessionKey, { integrationKey? })` | `void` |
| `sessions.list(provider, { integrationKey? })` | `Session[]` |
| `proxy.fetch(provider, path, ProxyRequest)` | `Response` (any provider status) |
| `proxy.enqueue(provider, path, ProxyRequest & { callbackUrl })` | `{ requestId }` |
| `webhooks.register(provider, { connectionKey, kind?, webhookKey?, metadata?, version?, body?, integrationKey? })` | `{ success, webhookKey, providerWebhookId?, kind? }` |
| `webhooks.list(provider, { connectionKey, integrationKey? })` | `Webhook[]` |
| `webhooks.get(provider, webhookKey, { connectionKey, integrationKey? })` | `Webhook` |
| `webhooks.update(provider, webhookKey, { connectionKey, body?, version?, integrationKey? })` | `{ success, webhookKey, … }` |
| `webhooks.delete(provider, webhookKey, { connectionKey, version?, integrationKey? })` | `{ success, webhookKey, … }` |
| `webhooks.initManual(provider, { connectionKey, redirectUrl?, integrationKey? })` | `{ sessionId, webhookKey, setupUrl, ingressUrl, status: 'pending', fields }` |
| `environment.integrations()` | `Integration[]` |
| `environment.identityProviders()` | `IdentityProvider[]` |

Standalone exports: `createPkce()` → `{ codeVerifier, codeChallenge, codeChallengeMethod: 'S256' }`;
`parseConnectionRedirect(url)` → `{ ok: true, connectionKey } | { ok: false, error, errorMessage }`
(`error` is `'missing_connection_key'` when the URL has neither param);
`verifyWebhook(headers, rawBody, secrets, opts?)`; `verifyResponse(response, secrets, opts?)`;
`verifySignature({ body, timestamp, signature, secrets, toleranceSeconds? })`.

Types: `Connection`, `Session`, `Webhook`, `Integration`, `IdentityProvider`, `UserInfo`,
`FormField`, `AuthType` (`oAuth1 | oAuth2 | api_key | basic | session`), `CredentialStatus`
(`active | pending | reauth_required | error | revoked | inactive`), `ProxyRequest`,
`SaltlineOptions`.

## Errors

```ts
import { SaltlineError } from '@aszura/saltline-node';

try {
  await saltline.connections.refresh('google', connectionKey);
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof SaltlineError) {
    error.status;    // HTTP status
    error.code;      // stable code; `HTTP_<status>` if none was sent
    error.requestId; // quote in support requests
    error.body;      // parsed JSON or raw text
  }
}
```

Common codes: `INVALID_API_KEY`, `API_KEY_EXPIRED`, `IP_NOT_ALLOWED`, `RATE_LIMITED`,
`LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, `CONFLICT` (refresh already running; retry shortly), `PROVIDER_NOT_FOUND`,
`INTEGRATION_NOT_FOUND`, `INTEGRATION_KEY_REQUIRED` (pass `integrationKey`),
`CONNECTION_NOT_FOUND`, `SESSION_NOT_FOUND`, `WEBHOOK_NOT_FOUND`, `MISSING_PKCE_PARAMETERS`,
`CODE_VERIFIER_MISMATCH` (wrong or reused verifier; start again), `AUTH_TYPE_NOT_SUPPORTED`,
`BLOCKED_PATH`. The full list is in `openapi.yaml` under `components.schemas.Error`.
